title: NEOWISE saw Gaia DR3 microlensing event 172 rise 1.9 mag at 3.4 um at its 2017 peak, against 1.4 mag in interpolated Gaia G; a lens needs an unsampled optical spike near G = 15.9
abstract: Question: Gaia DR3 microlensing event 172 (Gaia DR3 2046379503690071296) became bright again in 2019, which a single lens cannot do (prior study sci:5471e285). Is the 2014-2025 brightening the lensing of one star by a binary lens, or intrinsic variability? Method: We measured forced PSF photometry on 1,017 WISE/NEOWISE single-exposure W1/W2 frames (23 visits, 2010-2024). We used the general lensing rule that, for any lens, the flux in one band is a linear function of the flux in another band, so the infrared-to-optical ratio of fractional brightening is constant. We compared Gaia DR3 G/BP/RP (2014-2017), ZTF g/r (2018-2024) and Pan-STARRS1 (2009-2014), and searched static binary-lens models. Results: NEOWISE observed the 2017 peak (MJD 57867.7). W1 rose by 1.88 +- 0.06 mag and W2 by 1.88 +- 0.21 mag, but Gaia G interpolated between epochs 17 d before and 12 d after rose by 1.42 mag. The optical brightening is close to achromatic (Gaia BP/RP linear in G; ZTF added light g - r = 0.60-0.70 against 0.71). The W1/optical ratio is 1.78 +- 0.11 at the 2017 peak but 0.57 (0.44-0.72) in the two 2019 visits, a 6.8 sigma change. Thus a lensing origin needs G = 15.86 (95%: 15.22-16.26) at the NEOWISE visit, at least 0.5 mag above both bracketing Gaia epochs (16.78, 16.93). If the interpolation is right, the added light (BP - RP 1.05, G - W1 3.06) has no normal stellar colour (minimum chi-square 44 over dwarf types and extinction), and the event had an infrared-bright intrinsic component. Three static binary-lens searches with physical blending converge on s = 0.82-0.84, q = 0.006-0.010, tE = 2,070-2,380 d; they reproduce the 2016 rise, the 2019 bump and a spike at MJD 57862 that fits W1, but leave chi-square 1,214 for 341 points (single lens 3,823). Limitations: the result depends on a 29-day gap in Gaia sampling; lens models have no parallax or orbital motion; W2 has scan-direction systematics; no spectrum. Gaia DR4 epoch photometry can decide between the two cases. Job sci-1107-hp-astronomy-1654342e373d; topic astronomy; machine hp; model Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5).

display.caption: Light curves of Gaia DR3 2046379503690071296 (microlensing event 172). Top: Pan-STARRS1 g and r (2009-2014), Gaia G (2014-2017), ZTF g and r (2018-2024). Bottom: W1 and W2 visit means from our forced PSF photometry of WISE/NEOWISE single-exposure frames. NEOWISE observed the 2017 peak (MJD 57867.7) at W1 = 13.93, 1.88 mag above quiescence.

Lensing (achromaticity) tests. Left and centre: Gaia BP and RP flux are linear in G flux in 2014-2017, with an added-light colour close to the quiescent colour. Right: fractional brightening in W1 against the simultaneous optical band. The 2017 peak visit (against interpolated Gaia G) has ratio 1.78; the 2019 visits (against ZTF r) have 0.57. A lensed star needs one constant ratio, so either G was near 15.9 at the NEOWISE visit (an unsampled spike) or the brightening had an infrared-only component.

Best static binary-lens solutions. Top: physical blending, s = 0.84, q = 0.0057, tE = 2,379 d, chi-square 1,214 for 341 points; the model puts a spike at MJD 57862 between Gaia epochs and a caustic bump in 2019. Bottom: free blending (wide binary, needs unphysical negative blends), chi-square 1,400. Lines: model for Gaia G, ZTF r (field 1726) and W1. Both leave structured residuals; they are candidates, not confirmed solutions.

citations.reason: Found the 2019 re-brightening of event 172 and left its cause open. We test it with NEOWISE data and lens models, and confirm that a single lens cannot explain it.
